Receiving returned items.
Inspecting returned items.
Processing a refund or replacement.

result.rule: Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.

result.rule: When the description states that approval is followed by required activities and that the process closes after those activities: Connect the approval outcome through all required follow-up activities to the process end, preserving any ordering or parallelism stated in the description.

When the description says that one of several alternatives is selected, or that an activity may occur: Model the choice or optional activity with an appropriate gateway, and reconnect the resulting paths before subsequent common work.

When the description explicitly states that an actor performs an action that initiates the described process: Model the stated action as an activity in the actor’s scope; do not use a start event representing the resulting occurrence as a substitute for that activity. Represent the process start separately with an appropriate start event.

When the description makes an activity contingent on whether a stated condition holds: Model the condition with an exclusive gateway at the point where it affects the flow, and route the contingent activity only along the branch where the condition holds. Do not invent an outcome for the other branch.
